pharm: Third-generation cephalosporin; inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
summary: Cefpodoxime proxetil is an oral third-generation cephalosporin prodrug used for mild-to-moderate respiratory, urinary, skin, ear, and gonococcal infections. It is taken twice daily with food to improve absorption. Main cautions are beta-lactam hypersensitivity and antibiotic-associated C. difficile diarrhea.
indications: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis
Uncomplicated gonorrhea (urethral, cervical, ano-rectal in women)
admin: Take film-coated tablets orally with food to enhance absorption
Separate from high-dose antacids and H2 blockers (reduce absorption)
Complete the full prescribed course even if feeling better
Reserve for proven/strongly suspected bacterial infection
moa: Prodrug de-esterified to active cefpodoxime, which binds penicillin-binding proteins and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing bactericidal activity against many gram-positive and gram-negative organisms.

absolute: Known allergy to cefpodoxime or other cephalosporins
relative: History of penicillin/beta-lactam allergy (cross-reactivity up to ~10%)
monitor: Watch for diarrhea (possible C. difficile) up to 2 months after therapy
Signs of superinfection on prolonged use

preg: Category B; use only if clearly needed
lact: Excreted in milk (0-16% of serum); decide to stop nursing or drug
renal: CrCl <30 mL/min: extend interval to every 24 h; hemodialysis 3x/week after dialysis
hepatic: Cirrhosis PK similar to healthy; no dose adjustment needed

moderate: High-dose antacids (Na bicarbonate, aluminum hydroxide) reduce peak/absorption
minor: Oral anticholinergics (e.g. propantheline) delay time to peak
interactions.food: Take with food to increase absorption (AUC up 21-33%)
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine glucose with copper-reduction tests (cephalosporin class effect)

emergency: Anaphylaxis / severe acute hypersensitivity (needs epinephrine, airway support)
Pseudomembranous (C. difficile) colitis with watery/bloody stools

monitoring: Diarrhea / signs of C. difficile colitis during and after therapy
Renal function when given with nephrotoxic agents or diuretics
Signs of superinfection on prolonged use
counsel: Take with food at evenly spaced 12-hour intervals
Finish the entire course; do not skip doses
Antibiotics do not treat viral illness like the common cold
Report watery or bloody diarrhea, even weeks after stopping
Separate antacids and acid-reducers from this medicine
pearls: Prodrug: cefpodoxime proxetil is de-esterified to active cefpodoxime after absorption
Absorption is improved with food (tablets) and reduced by antacids/H2 blockers
Beta-lactam cross-hypersensitivity may occur in up to 10% of penicillin-allergic patients
Skin/skin-structure infections require the higher 400 mg twice-daily dose
Single 200 mg dose treats uncomplicated gonorrhea; not for pharyngeal gonococcal infection
missed: Take when remembered; skip if near next dose, do not double
overdose: Nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress, diarrhea; supportive care; dialysis may aid removal
